spans.title: The Suspicious Major
spans.blurb: Travelers land on a coast plagued by pirates and meet a planter leaning on a monstrous rifle. Breakfast or a bullet depends on what he decides they are.

spans.title: Who Made God?
spans.blurb: A boy certain of scripture meets one question he cannot answer. Within an hour his whole spiritual world lies in ruins, and something unexpected rises in its place.

spans.title: The Night Chicago Burned
spans.blurb: A city burns to the waterline while thousands camp on the lakeshore. One young drover races to save a herd of cattle and discovers what people are made of.

books.pairNote: Two unrelated episodes, a boyhood crisis of faith and the great fire, that coexist without touching.

spans.title: The Dog at the Door
spans.blurb: A sailor fresh from an Indian voyage stops for a shave on Fleet Street. His dog takes one look at the barber and refuses to leave the door.

spans.title: The Square Cop
spans.blurb: A policeman swears he is on the square. The Commissioner tests him with a sneer, then hands him orders that no honest man could stomach.

spans.title: Playing the Game
spans.blurb: A wife asks her barrister husband for her freedom. He names one condition, and she must choose between a single easy lie and the truth that costs everything.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that Aliette admits an attachment and that her husband refuses her a divorce, a central mid-book turning point.

spans.title: An Ear for an Ear
spans.blurb: A king pardons the stray arrow that takes his ear. Then shipwreck, murder, and a stranger's blood on his clothes leave his life hanging on one lucky throw.

spans.title: Take Away That Bauble
spans.blurb: A grandly eloquent bucket shop manager mistakes two young motorists for college boys with pocket money to lose. They let him keep believing it.

spans.title: I Hate Being Involved
spans.blurb: A gentleman devoted to his club, his bridge, and his comfort explains why he hates being involved in anything, just as a telegram arrives to involve him.

spans.title: The Dancer's Whip Hand
spans.blurb: After her triumph, a dancer receives an elegant visitor and confides her plan: she alone holds the whip hand over the mastermind they both serve.

books.pairNote: The diary sketch and the dressing room scene share no text, characters, or reveals.

spans.title: Deduce, Poirot!
spans.blurb: From a window over a London street, one friend spins a drama of crooks and shadowers below. The other simply rises to look for himself.

spans.title: Going Back to Grandma
spans.blurb: Three years old and done with it all, a small girl announces she is leaving home for Grandma's. Between her and the way stands a black embankment.
